description: A full 78-card tarot deck reimagined through the lens of cricket. 22 Major Arcana of the game's rituals and turning points, plus 56 Minor Arcana across four suits: Bats (drive and ambition), Caps (feeling and belonging), Seam (mind and conflict), and Stumps (graft and results). Each suit runs Ace to Ten plus four court cards: the Colt, the Quick, the Senior Pro, and the Great.

Bats.theme: drive, ambition, momentum, enterprise, attacking intent

Seam.theme: mind, strategy, conflict, hard truths, communication

Stumps.theme: graft, results, security, the body, the tangible

courts.The Colt: Page — the learner, the fresh prospect, curiosity and news
courts.The Quick: Knight — the mover, pursuit and momentum, action for better or worse
courts.The Senior Pro: Queen — mastery held inward, the dressing-room voice, leading by example
courts.The Great: King — mastery turned outward, command, authority and legacy

cards.name: The Debutant
cards.cricketMeaning: Walking out to bat or bowl for the very first time, cap on, heart pounding, everything still to prove.
cards.upright: A fresh start is here. Trust your instincts even though you haven't 'earned' the moment yet — everyone starts with a first over, a first innings. Take the guard and back yourself.
cards.reversed: Recklessness or hesitation at the crease. You're either charging in without a plan or too scared to leave the changing room. Find the middle ground before you play the shot.

cards.name: The Allrounder
cards.cricketMeaning: The player who can bat, bowl, and field with equal skill — turning whatever is at hand into a match-winning performance.
cards.upright: You have everything you need already. Skills, timing, and opportunity are aligning — it's time to contribute with bat and ball, not wait to be picked for one role.
cards.reversed: Spreading yourself too thin, or talent without application. A gifted player who never quite delivers. Focus on one skill and sharpen it.

cards.name: The Wicketkeeper
cards.cricketMeaning: Standing behind the stumps, saying little, seeing everything — the game's quiet intelligence.
cards.upright: Listen more than you speak. The answer you need isn't in noise or analysis — it's in the quiet read you already have on the situation. Trust the instinct behind the stumps.
cards.reversed: Ignoring your gut, or overthinking a simple appeal. You're second-guessing what you already know. Go back to instinct.

cards.name: The Home Ground
cards.cricketMeaning: A flat pitch, a friendly crowd, familiar conditions — everything set up for you to flourish.
cards.upright: Conditions favor you right now. Let yourself be supported, grow into the innings, and don't rush what's naturally building in your favor.
cards.reversed: Home comfort turning into complacency, or a supportive environment being taken for granted. Don't let easy conditions make you lazy.

cards.name: The Captain
cards.cricketMeaning: The one setting the field, making the calls, carrying the weight of every decision.
cards.upright: Step up and take control. A situation needs your structure and decisiveness — set the field, make the call, own the outcome.
cards.reversed: Over-control or rigid captaincy that stifles the team. You're micromanaging the field instead of trusting your bowlers. Loosen the grip.

cards.name: The Coach
cards.cricketMeaning: The voice in the nets reminding you of technique, discipline, and the basics that never go out of style.
cards.upright: Go back to fundamentals. A mentor, a coaching manual, or plain old discipline has the answer you're looking for. Respect the process.
cards.reversed: Blindly following outdated advice, or rejecting all guidance out of stubbornness. Question the method, but don't throw out the technique entirely.

cards.name: The Partnership
cards.cricketMeaning: Two batsmen at the crease, running on trust, building something neither could alone.
cards.upright: A relationship or collaboration is at a turning point — commit to it fully. Communicate clearly, run the singles, trust your partner.
cards.reversed: A breakdown in communication — a mix-up, a run-out waiting to happen. Miscommunication is the real danger here, not the opposition.

cards.name: The Chase
cards.cricketMeaning: Batting under lights, required run rate climbing, nothing but forward momentum and nerve.
cards.upright: Full steam ahead. You have the drive to pull this off — stay focused on the target and don't let doubt slow your running between the wickets.
cards.reversed: Losing control of the chase — panicking, changing plans mid-over, or trying to do too much too fast. Reset and rebuild the required rate calmly.

cards.name: The Anchor
cards.cricketMeaning: The batsman who holds one end steady through a collapse, absorbing pressure without flinching.
cards.upright: Real strength here is calm, not aggression. Hold your position, absorb the pressure, and let the storm around you pass without losing your composure.
cards.reversed: Forcing control through stubbornness, or crumbling under pressure you tried to just 'tough out.' Strength without patience becomes brittle.

cards.name: The Twelfth Man
cards.cricketMeaning: Watching from the boundary, drinks tray in hand, learning the game from the outside looking in.
cards.upright: Step back and observe before acting. This is a season for quiet reflection, not center stage — your moment will come, use this time to prepare.
cards.reversed: Isolating yourself when you should be engaging, or feeling permanently overlooked. Don't mistake being benched for being forgotten.

cards.name: The Toss
cards.cricketMeaning: The coin spinning in the air before a ball is bowled — fortune's first, unearned decision of the day.
cards.upright: Circumstances beyond your control are about to shift. A change of luck is coming — win or lose the toss, what matters is how you play the conditions you're given.
cards.reversed: A run of bad luck, or blaming fortune for outcomes you could still influence. The toss is only the start of the story, not the whole match.

cards.name: The Umpire
cards.cricketMeaning: The final word on every appeal — impartial, deliberate, bound by the laws of the game.
cards.upright: A fair and honest decision is needed, from you or about you. Trust the process, accept the outcome, and act with integrity even when it costs you.
cards.reversed: An unfair call, or refusing to accept a decision that's already been made. Dwelling on a bad decision only costs you the next ball.

cards.name: The Rain Delay
cards.cricketMeaning: Covers on, players off, the match suspended in limbo — nothing to do but wait and see it differently.
cards.upright: Progress is paused for a reason. Use this stoppage to see the situation from a new angle rather than fighting the delay. Sometimes waiting is the move.
cards.reversed: Resisting a necessary pause, or staying stuck in limbo long after play could resume. Don't let the delay become an excuse to stall.

cards.name: The Run Out
cards.cricketMeaning: Gone in an instant, no warning, no half-measures — one end of something, the start of another.
cards.upright: An abrupt ending is clearing space for what's next. Don't fight the finish — a chapter is closing so a new innings can begin.
cards.reversed: Refusing to accept something is over, dragging out an ending that's already happened. Walk off before you're given out.

cards.name: The Declaration
cards.cricketMeaning: The captain choosing exactly the right moment to stop batting — not too early, not too greedy.
cards.upright: Balance and good timing matter more than pushing for more. You have enough — declare, and set up the next phase from a position of strength.
cards.reversed: Bad timing — declaring too early out of impatience, or batting on too long out of greed. Reassess what 'enough' actually looks like.

cards.name: The Sledge
cards.cricketMeaning: Words from the slip cordon designed to get in your head — a test of what you'll let control you.
cards.upright: Something is baiting your ego — a rivalry, a grudge, a bad habit dressed up as competitive fire. Notice what's pulling your focus off the game.
cards.reversed: Breaking free from a temptation or toxic pattern that's had a grip on you. You're learning to let the sledging go unanswered.

cards.name: The Collapse
cards.cricketMeaning: Five wickets in five overs — the innings falling apart faster than anyone expected.
cards.upright: A sudden, disruptive event is dismantling something that looked stable. It's disorienting, but it's clearing out what wasn't built to last anyway.
cards.reversed: Fearing a collapse that hasn't happened yet, or narrowly avoiding one. Don't let anxiety about falling apart cost you the innings that's still in front of you.

cards.name: The Comeback
cards.cricketMeaning: Returning to the field after injury or a lean patch, quietly rebuilding form and belief.
cards.upright: Hope is well placed here. After a difficult stretch, healing and form are genuinely returning — trust the quiet signs of recovery.
cards.reversed: Losing faith just before the turnaround, or rushing the comeback before you're truly ready. Give the recovery the time it needs.

cards.name: The Floodlights
cards.cricketMeaning: A day-night match under lights and dew — the ball behaving strangely, nothing quite as it seems.
cards.upright: Things aren't fully clear right now, and that's okay. Move carefully through the uncertainty rather than assuming you can read conditions you can't yet see.
cards.reversed: Confusion lifting, or anxiety about the unknown that's bigger than the situation warrants. The dew will settle — don't panic-bowl at shadows.

cards.name: The Century
cards.cricketMeaning: Bat raised to the crowd, three figures on the board — pure, uncomplicated triumph.
cards.upright: Genuine success and joy are here, earned and deserved. Let yourself enjoy this moment fully — no caveats needed.
cards.reversed: Success that feels hollow, or joy you're not allowing yourself to feel. Don't undersell a century just because it wasn't a double.

cards.name: The Review
cards.cricketMeaning: Bat tucked under the arm, waiting on the big screen — a decision from the past being revisited and made right.
cards.upright: A past decision is being reconsidered, and you may get the reprieve you've been hoping for. Trust the review process and be honest about what really happened.
cards.reversed: Refusing to review your own mistakes, or burning a review on false hope. Be honest with yourself before you ask for a second look.

cards.name: The World Cup
cards.cricketMeaning: The trophy lifted, the long tournament finally complete — everything you worked for, whole and realized.
cards.upright: A long cycle is reaching genuine completion. Whatever you've been building toward has arrived — take it in before starting the next campaign.
cards.reversed: Something close to completion but not quite there — a final short of the boundary. Don't stop chasing just before the finish line.

cards.name: Ace of Bats
cards.cricketMeaning: The ball middled straight back past the bowler off the first delivery — a jolt of pure intent, an innings that wants to happen.
cards.upright: A burst of energy and ambition is being handed to you. Something wants to be started. Don't overthink it — take guard and swing through the line.
cards.reversed: A false start, or drive with nowhere to go. You're fired up but swinging at everything, or the spark's fizzled before you left the crease. Wait for a ball worth playing.

cards.name: Two of Bats
cards.cricketMeaning: Standing at the crease after one solid shot, looking around the field, deciding how the innings is going to be built.
cards.upright: You've made the first move and now you're mapping the rest. This is the moment to choose your approach deliberately rather than just reacting ball to ball.
cards.reversed: Analysis paralysis at the crease. You're so busy planning the perfect innings that you're playing every ball for time. Pick a plan and commit.

cards.name: Three of Bats
cards.cricketMeaning: Mid-innings, the running is sharp, the gaps are opening, and you can see the total you're heading for.
cards.upright: Early effort is starting to pay off. Keep looking for the singles and trust that what you've set in motion is coming good. Support is closer than you think.
cards.reversed: Plans stalling, a partner not backing up, momentum leaking away. Something you expected to arrive hasn't. Check what's actually holding it up before you push harder.

cards.name: Four of Bats
keywords: the dressing room on its feet
cards.cricketMeaning: The fifty raised, bat lifted to a standing pavilion, a partnership that's given the innings a proper foundation.
cards.upright: A stable, happy milestone. Take the applause, enjoy the homecoming, and appreciate the base you've built with people around you.
cards.reversed: The celebration feels thinner than it should, or there's tension behind the smiles in the camp. Mark the milestone honestly rather than performing it.

cards.name: Five of Bats
cards.cricketMeaning: A net session that's turned into a contest, every batter wanting the throwdowns, everyone talking over each other.
cards.upright: Lots of competing energy and no clear order. It's messy, maybe even useful, but nothing gets built while everyone's fighting for the strike. Sort out who's on first.
cards.reversed: The squabble is either winding down or curdling into something personal. Decide which, and either make peace or step out of the net.

cards.name: Six of Bats
cards.cricketMeaning: Carried off the ground on teammates' shoulders, the match-winning knock behind you, the crowd on their feet.
cards.upright: Public recognition you've genuinely earned. Accept it without deflecting — this is a moment of visible success and it's allowed to feel good.
cards.reversed: A win that rings false, praise you don't quite trust, or credit going to the wrong person. Check whether the acclaim matches the reality.

cards.name: Seven of Bats
cards.cricketMeaning: Last recognised batter, farming the strike, shielding the tail while the opposition throws everything at you.
cards.upright: You're defending something and the odds are against you, but you have the higher ground. Stand firm, keep your shape, and make them earn every wicket.
cards.reversed: Worn down by the constant pressure, tempted to just give it away. Either dig back in properly or accept it's time to change your approach — half-defending helps no one.

cards.name: Eight of Bats
cards.cricketMeaning: The ball racing to the boundary, sharp singles turned into twos, everything happening at pace.
cards.upright: Things are moving fast and in your favour. Decisions land, messages arrive, the run rate climbs. Keep up and run hard — this window won't stay open long.
cards.reversed: Rushed shots and mix-ups. The pace has got away from you and you're playing catch-up. Slow the over down before someone gets run out.

cards.name: Nine of Bats
cards.cricketMeaning: Bruised on the arm and thigh, helmet dented, playing and missing — but still there, still guarding the stumps.
cards.upright: You've taken a battering and you're tired, but you're closer to the end of this than you think. Get behind one more ball. Don't give it away with the finish line in sight.
cards.reversed: Paranoia at the crease, flinching before the ball's bowled, refusing help out of exhaustion. The war's in your head now more than on the pitch. Ask someone to bat with you.

cards.name: Ten of Bats
keywords: the weight of doing it all
cards.cricketMeaning: Batting through the entire innings, bowling first change, keeping wicket in a pinch — dragging the team along on your own.
cards.upright: You're carrying more than one person should. The job's nearly done, so finish it — but notice that you took all of this on yourself, and ask whether you had to.
cards.reversed: The load is crushing you and it's time to put some of it down. Delegate, drop what isn't essential, or admit the innings can't all be yours.

cards.name: The Colt of Bats
cards.cricketMeaning: A raw academy slogger with more enthusiasm than plan, desperate to get out there and have a go.
cards.upright: An exciting idea or piece of news is arriving, still rough but full of life. Follow the enthusiasm and see where it leads before you talk yourself out of it.
cards.reversed: All talk and no footwork. Big declarations, restless energy, nothing actually started. Turn one of those ideas into a single concrete action.

cards.name: The Quick of Bats
cards.cricketMeaning: Dances down the pitch to the quick bowler and launches it over long-on — thrilling, fearless, and one bad ball from disaster.
cards.upright: Time for a bold, committed move. Back yourself and go hard at the opportunity. Just make sure you've picked the right ball to attack.
cards.reversed: Recklessness dressed up as courage. Haring off in a new direction, burning hot and fading, leaving chaos behind. Channel the drive into something you'll still want tomorrow.

cards.name: The Senior Pro of Bats
cards.cricketMeaning: An attacking veteran who still takes bowlers apart and lights up the dressing room just by walking in.
cards.upright: Lead with warmth and self-assurance. People follow this energy naturally — set the tone by how you play, not by what you demand.
cards.reversed: Dominating the room, taking the game away from teammates, needing to be the one who wins it. Make space for others to have a bat.

cards.name: The Great of Bats
keywords: setting the tone for a campaign
cards.cricketMeaning: A batting legend who maps out a whole series in his head and makes the entire side believe it's possible.
cards.upright: You can see the big picture and rally people to it. Lead decisively, set an ambitious direction, and trust others to fill in the detail.
cards.reversed: Impatient, ruling by ego, all attack and no plan. Vision without follow-through, or a leader who won't hear a second opinion. Slow down and listen.

cards.name: Ace of Caps
cards.cricketMeaning: The first cap handed over before your debut, throat tight during the anthem — belonging offered, freely.
cards.upright: A new feeling, relationship, or sense of belonging is being offered to you. Let yourself receive it. Say yes to the connection before you rationalise it away.
cards.reversed: Feelings held back, an offer you can't quite accept, the anthem falling flat. Something's blocking the flow. Notice whether you're the one holding the tap shut.

cards.name: Two of Caps
cards.cricketMeaning: Two players walking out to bat together, touching gloves mid-pitch, completely in each other's corner.
cards.upright: A genuine partnership — even, honest, mutual. Whether it's new love, a friendship, or peace made with a rival, both sides are pulling the same way.
cards.reversed: A partnership out of sync, a run-out between two people who should trust each other. The connection's real but the communication's off. Talk before you run.

cards.name: Three of Caps
cards.cricketMeaning: The whole side in a huddle at the close, arms round shoulders, belting out the team song.
cards.upright: Lean into your people. This is a time for celebration, community, and letting friends carry you along. A win shared is worth more.
cards.reversed: The huddle that leaves someone on the outside, or one too many nights out papering over something real. Check who's not in the circle, and why.

cards.name: Four of Caps
cards.cricketMeaning: Sitting on the boundary rope, arms folded, turning down a game of beach cricket because you can't be bothered.
cards.upright: You're so flat or so used to what you have that you're not seeing an offer right in front of you. Look up. Someone's holding out a cap.
cards.reversed: Coming out of the slump. The restlessness is lifting and you're ready to say yes to things again. Take the next invitation.

cards.name: Five of Caps
cards.cricketMeaning: Three catches shelled in a session, standing at slip staring at the grass, forgetting there are still catches to come.
cards.upright: You're focused on what's been lost or dropped. The disappointment is fair — but two chances are still standing behind you. Don't let the spilled ones cost you those too.
cards.reversed: Turning around to face what's still there. Acceptance is starting, the grief is loosening its grip. Pick the ball up and get ready for the next one.

cards.name: Six of Caps
cards.cricketMeaning: Playing tapeball in the garden with the kids and a couple of old teammates, the game stripped back to pure fun.
cards.upright: Something warm from the past is worth revisiting — an old friend, a simpler version of the game, an act of kindness returned. Let it in.
cards.reversed: Living in the glory days, unable to bring that warmth into the present. Honour the memory, then come back to the innings you're actually playing.

cards.name: Seven of Caps
cards.cricketMeaning: Staring at a wall of offers — county deals, franchise contracts, a coaching role — half of them mirages.
cards.upright: You have options, but some of them are fantasy. Get concrete: which of these actually exists, and which are you just enjoying imagining? Then choose one.
cards.reversed: The fog is clearing and one path is becoming obviously right. Commitment is close. Stop window-shopping and sign.

cards.name: Eight of Caps
cards.cricketMeaning: Packing your kit and leaving a club you love because something essential just isn't there anymore.
cards.upright: It's time to walk away from something that looks fine on paper but has quietly stopped feeding you. This is a brave, sad, necessary exit — make it cleanly.
cards.reversed: Staying out of fear, or bolting before you've really understood what's missing. Be honest about whether you're leaving or just running.

cards.name: Nine of Caps
cards.cricketMeaning: Feet up in the rooms after a match-winning innings, cold drink in hand, the day gone exactly as you'd have written it.
cards.upright: A wish is coming good and you're allowed to enjoy it. Take the satisfaction of a job done well — this is the pleasant, well-fed version of success.
cards.reversed: Smugness, or a wish that came true and didn't fill you up. Ask whether you were chasing the right thing, or just the look of it.

cards.name: Ten of Caps
cards.cricketMeaning: The whole club at the ground on a summer evening — players, families, juniors, sunset behind the sightscreen, everyone at home.
cards.upright: Emotional fulfilment that lasts, not just a good day. The relationships around you are solid and nourishing. This is what you were building toward.
cards.reversed: A picture-perfect setup with a hairline crack in it. The harmony is mostly real — tend to the small thing that isn't before it spreads.

cards.name: The Colt of Caps
cards.cricketMeaning: A young player who feels the game deeply and leaves a handwritten note of thanks in a senior's kit bag.
cards.upright: A tender, creative, or sincere message is arriving — or wants to be sent by you. Follow the feeling even if it seems a bit soft. It'll land well.
cards.reversed: Moodiness, over-sensitivity, or a message you keep drafting and never send. The feeling's valid; the sulking isn't helping. Say the thing.

cards.name: The Quick of Caps
keywords: following the heart onto the field
cards.cricketMeaning: A bowler chasing the one perfect spell of swing, playing on feel, turning up with a proposal in his eyes.
cards.upright: An offer or invitation led by feeling rather than logic is on its way. It's charming and sincere. Meet it with an open mind — just keep one foot on the ground.
cards.reversed: Grand romantic gestures built on air, promises that outrun reality, moods swinging the plan around. Ask for the substance behind the sweetness.

cards.name: The Senior Pro of Caps
keywords: the heart of the dressing room
cards.cricketMeaning: The player who always knows who's struggling before they say a word, and quietly sits next to them.
cards.upright: Lead with empathy. Your ability to read and hold other people's feelings is the strength here — use it, and trust your own emotional read of the situation.
cards.reversed: Carrying everyone else's weight until you're underwater, or using care as control. Put your own pads on first.

cards.name: The Great of Caps
cards.cricketMeaning: A veteran captain who stays serene when the chase gets tight and settles every dispute in the room without raising his voice.
cards.upright: Steady, warm authority. You can feel everything that's going on and still keep your head. Lead the emotional temperature of the group down, not up.
cards.reversed: Calm on the surface, churning underneath — or using that composure to manipulate. Let someone see what you're actually feeling.

cards.name: Ace of Seam
cards.cricketMeaning: A delivery that pitches leg and hits the top of off — the unplayable ball, the truth that can't be argued with.
cards.upright: A moment of hard, clean clarity. You suddenly see the situation for what it is. Act on that insight now, while it's sharp, and say the true thing plainly.
cards.reversed: Muddled thinking, a clever plan that misfires, or using the truth like a bouncer aimed at the head. Get your own reasoning straight before you deliver it.

cards.name: Two of Seam
cards.cricketMeaning: Batter dug in on the back foot, playing everything with a dead bat, refusing to commit forward or back.
cards.upright: You're avoiding a choice by blocking every ball. It feels safe but the over isn't moving. You have more information than you're admitting — use it and decide.
cards.reversed: The deadlock breaks. A fact you were shutting out gets through, and the choice makes itself. Uncomfortable, but a relief.

cards.name: Three of Seam
cards.cricketMeaning: Middle stump cartwheeling out of the ground, no doubt about it, the long walk back with the crowd silent.
cards.upright: Something hurts and there's no spinning it — a rejection, a betrayal, a hard piece of feedback that's landed. Feel it properly. Pretending you weren't bowled won't help.
cards.reversed: The sharpest of the pain is passing. You're starting to release the grievance and get back to the nets. Don't rush the healing, but do let it begin.

cards.name: Four of Seam
cards.cricketMeaning: Sitting out a session with the pads still on, lying back in a quiet corner of the rooms, letting the mind go still.
cards.upright: Stop. You need genuine rest before the next passage of play — not a holiday, just quiet. Step out of the contest and recover, guilt-free.
cards.reversed: Restlessness, or forcing yourself back onto the field before you've recovered. Either you won't let yourself rest or you've rested long enough — be honest which.

cards.name: Five of Seam
cards.cricketMeaning: Out-sledging the opposition all day and winning the game, then noticing your own dressing room has gone quiet.
cards.upright: You can win this argument, but count what it costs. A victory that leaves you isolated or the other person humiliated isn't worth much. Choose your battle.
cards.reversed: A chance to make amends after a fight that got out of hand. Someone's ready to walk it back — you can be the one who offers first.

cards.name: Six of Seam
cards.cricketMeaning: A quiet mid-season move to a new county, gear in the boot, heading somewhere the pitches are kinder.
cards.upright: You're moving away from a rough patch toward calmer water. It's not dramatic and you're not fully okay yet, but the direction is right. Keep going.
cards.reversed: Carrying the baggage with you, or a move that doesn't actually solve anything. Work out what you need to leave behind before you pack the car.

cards.name: Seven of Seam
cards.cricketMeaning: Copying the opposition's bowling plans off the analyst's laptop while no one's watching, and slipping out unseen.
cards.upright: A situation calls for cleverness and discretion rather than a frontal contest. Move quietly, keep your own counsel — but be honest with yourself about whether this is smart or just sneaky.
cards.reversed: A scheme unravelling, or getting caught. The quiet approach has stopped working. Come clean before someone else does it for you.

cards.name: Eight of Seam
cards.cricketMeaning: Padded up in the pavilion, certain you can't bat on this surface — while the gate stands open and nobody's stopping you.
cards.upright: You feel boxed in, but most of the walls are in your head. List what's actually preventing you versus what you've just decided is impossible. The way out is closer than it looks.
cards.reversed: You're starting to see the exit. One assumption falls away and suddenly there's room to move. Take the first step out.

cards.name: Nine of Seam
cards.cricketMeaning: Lying awake the night before a Test, replaying every dismissal you've ever had, each one worse in the dark.
cards.upright: Worry has taken over and it's bigger at night than the situation deserves. Write the fears down, say them out loud to someone. Most of them shrink in daylight.
cards.reversed: The worst of the dread is breaking. You're reaching out, getting perspective, realising the monster was mostly shadow. Keep talking about it.

cards.name: Ten of Seam
cards.cricketMeaning: All ten wickets down, the innings folded for next to nothing, the scorecard a disaster — and nothing worse left to happen.
cards.upright: Something has ended badly and completely. It stings, but there's a strange relief in the finality: you can stop bracing now. The only way from here is up.
cards.reversed: A slow climb out of the wreckage, or a refusal to accept the innings is finished. Let it be over so you can start the next one.

cards.name: The Colt of Seam
cards.cricketMeaning: A sharp-eyed young player who watches every opposition net and isn't shy about saying what he's spotted.
cards.upright: Stay alert and ask the pointed questions. New information is coming and it may be delivered bluntly. Gather facts before you form the plan.
cards.reversed: Gossip, spying, words used to cut rather than clarify. Sharp for the sake of it. Check your motive before you pass that on.

cards.name: The Quick of Seam
cards.cricketMeaning: An express bowler who bangs the ball in short and backs it with a stare — all aggression, all forward.
cards.upright: Charge at the problem directly and fast. This is a moment for bold, uncompromising action. Just aim it — raw pace with no line goes for four.
cards.reversed: Aggression with no plan, steamrolling people, saying the cutting thing and calling it honesty. Slow your run-up and pick your target.

cards.name: The Senior Pro of Seam
cards.cricketMeaning: The unsentimental senior who tells you exactly why you're getting out, whether you want to hear it or not.
cards.upright: Think clearly and speak straight. Cut sentiment out of the decision and see the situation as it is. Set the boundary you've been avoiding.
cards.reversed: Coldness, cutting remarks, a hardness that's tipped from honest into bitter. Clarity is still the goal — warmth doesn't have to be the price.

cards.name: The Great of Seam
cards.cricketMeaning: A captain who leads by intellect and the laws of the game — brilliant, exacting, never plays favourites.
cards.upright: Lead with principle and logic. Make the fair call even when it's unpopular, hold the standard, and let the truth do the work rather than your rank.
cards.reversed: Harsh judgement, rule for rule's sake, using the truth as a weapon and calling it fairness. Ask whether you're being just or just being right.

cards.name: Ace of Stumps
cards.cricketMeaning: A first professional contract slid across the table, or the keys to a ground of your own — something solid to build on.
cards.upright: A concrete, practical opportunity is here: a job, a deal, a resource, a foundation. It's real and it has legs. Plant it properly and tend it.
cards.reversed: A shaky offer, a good opening missed, or a plan with no ground under it. Check whether the opportunity is as solid as it looks before you commit.

cards.name: Two of Stumps
cards.cricketMeaning: Holding down a day job, club cricket, and training, keeping every ball in the air with a grin.
cards.upright: You're balancing a lot and, for now, handling it. Stay light on your feet and keep prioritising ball by ball. Don't add a fourth thing to juggle.
cards.reversed: A ball's about to drop. You've overcommitted and the plates are wobbling. Decide what you're allowed to put down before it chooses for you.

cards.name: Three of Stumps
cards.cricketMeaning: Groundstaff, coach and captain crouched over the square together, each trade respected, planning the surface.
cards.upright: Good collaborative work where everyone's expertise counts. Ask for input, take the craft seriously, and build it to last. Your skill is being noticed.
cards.reversed: Cut corners, no one aligned, work done to just-about-passable. Slow down and get the people who know what they're doing back in the room.

cards.name: Four of Stumps
cards.cricketMeaning: Guarding your batting average, blocking every single delivery, refusing any shot that carries the slightest risk.
cards.upright: You're protecting what you've got — savings, a position, a reputation. Some caution is wise. But an innings of pure defence never wins a game.
cards.reversed: Clutching so hard nothing can flow — money, control, feelings. The grip itself has become the problem. Play one attacking shot and see that the sky doesn't fall.

cards.name: Five of Stumps
keywords: feeling left out in the cold
cards.cricketMeaning: Dropped off the contract list, kit bag on the pavement outside the members' bar, the warm room just the other side of the glass.
cards.upright: A stretch of real insecurity — money, work, health, or belonging. It's genuinely hard. But look around: there's help nearby, and asking for it isn't losing.
cards.reversed: Coming in from the cold. The lean patch is easing, support has been found, or you've finally knocked on the door. Recovery is underway.

cards.name: Six of Stumps
cards.cricketMeaning: A senior pro quietly paying for a young player's kit and travel, no fuss, no scoreboard kept.
cards.upright: Help is flowing in a fair direction — you're either well placed to give it or right to accept it. Keep the exchange clean and even.
cards.reversed: Strings attached, uneven giving, a favour held over your head. Check what the generosity is really costing before you take it — or before you offer it that way.

cards.name: Seven of Stumps
cards.cricketMeaning: Leaning on the bat handle at mid-pitch between overs, looking at a season's graft, weighing whether to stick with it.
cards.upright: Step back and honestly assess what your effort has grown so far. It may not be ready to harvest yet — patience is probably the answer, but check the plant is actually healthy.
cards.reversed: Impatience, or pulling out of a long investment right before it pays. Alternatively, throwing more time at something that was never going to grow. Be honest about which.

cards.name: Eight of Stumps
cards.cricketMeaning: Alone in the nets at dusk, grooving the same cover drive a thousand times until it's muscle memory.
cards.upright: Put the reps in. This is a time for focused, patient practice of your craft — unglamorous, repetitive, and exactly how the skill gets built. Keep going.
cards.reversed: Going through the motions, or perfectionism with no purpose. Either the work has gone soulless or you're polishing something no one needs polished. Reconnect it to the point.

cards.name: Nine of Stumps
cards.cricketMeaning: A well-deserved benefit year, strolling the outfield of a ground you helped build, comfortable in your own company.
cards.upright: You've done the work and now you get to enjoy what it produced — comfort, self-sufficiency, a bit of well-earned ease. Let yourself have it.
cards.reversed: Comfort that cost more than it was worth, or restlessness in the middle of plenty. Check whether the independence you fought for is actually the life you wanted.

cards.name: Ten of Stumps
cards.cricketMeaning: Three generations of the same family on the honours board, the pavilion named after a grandfather, the club an institution.
cards.upright: Long-term security and continuity — wealth, tradition, something built to outlast you. Think about what you're passing on, not just what you're holding.
cards.reversed: Legacy as a weight, family expectation as a cage, money without meaning. Honour where you came from without letting it bat your innings for you.

cards.name: The Colt of Stumps
cards.cricketMeaning: A diligent young pro rewatching footage late into the night, notebook full, in no rush and missing nothing.
cards.upright: A chance to learn something concrete or start something real is here. Do the homework, take it step by step, and treat the small opportunity seriously.
cards.reversed: Procrastination, all study and no time in the middle, or a plan that stays a plan forever. Set the books down and face a ball.

cards.name: The Quick of Stumps
cards.cricketMeaning: A metronomic seamer who lands it on a coin all day, never spectacular, never collared, always exactly where you need him.
cards.upright: Slow, steady, dependable progress. Not exciting, but it works. Keep hitting your spot over after over and the job gets done.
cards.reversed: Stuck in the same groove past the point it's useful, resisting any change to the routine. Reliability has curdled into a rut. Try a different length.

cards.name: The Senior Pro of Stumps
cards.cricketMeaning: The veteran who makes sure the young players are fed, housed, and match-ready, and still scores runs on Saturday.
cards.upright: Look after the practical needs — yours and the group's. Be resourceful, keep the environment secure and well-run, and lead by keeping everyone standing.
cards.reversed: So focused on results and logistics that the people get treated like line items. Provision without warmth. Ask how everyone's actually doing.

cards.name: The Great of Stumps
cards.cricketMeaning: A shrewd club-builder who took a struggling side, balanced the books, laid the square, and turned it into an institution.
cards.upright: You have the standing and the resources to build something durable. Lead with discipline and generosity, invest for the long term, and provide for the people who rely on you.
cards.reversed: Greed, status obsession, controlling people through money and security. Wealth hoarded rather than put to work. Loosen the grip and remember what it's for.
